_comment: Declarative risk signals for the pr-risk-review skill. Shared by every agent
that runs the skill (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Copilot coding agent) so
the heuristic half of a review is identical no matter who runs it.
Paths are glob patterns matched against repo-relative POSIX paths.
'*' matches within one segment, '**' crosses segments, '**/' also matches zero segments.

sizeThresholds._comment: Changed lines (insertions + deletions) and file counts that push the baseline up on their own.

_comment: A file matching one of these is treated as low-risk however deep in the
tree it sits — `vscode-extension/src/test/foo.test.ts` is a test first and a
host integration second. Their lines are also excluded from the size
thresholds, so 2,000 lines of markdown never reads as a 2,000-line review.
Keep the globs for these categories narrow: anything they match stops

generatedPaths._comment: Counted separately from hand-written code — a 20k-line lockfile churn is not a 20k-line review.

categories.label: CI / supply chain
categories.why: Workflow and action changes execute with repository credentials. A change here can exfiltrate secrets, publish artifacts, or push to protected branches — review the permissions block, the trigger, and every third-party action SHA.

categories.label: Secrets / authentication
categories.why: Touches authentication, session handling, or credential material. Confirm no secret is logged, no auth check is weakened, and no default grants more access than before.

categories.label: Infrastructure / deployment
categories.why: Terraform, container, and deployment definitions change live infrastructure. Confirm the plan is reversible and no resource is replaced or destroyed unintentionally.

categories.label: Publishing / release
categories.why: Feeds the marketplace, npm, and plugin-portal publishing paths. A mistake ships to users and cannot be unpublished cleanly.

categories.label: Shared core logic
categories.why: `src/` is consumed by the VS Code extension AND the CLI (and through them the Visual Studio and JetBrains hosts). A regression here is multiplied across every host — session parsing, token estimation, and cost attribution all live behind these modules.

categories.label: Cost / pricing data
categories.why: Drives money numbers shown to users. A wrong entry silently misattributes cost instead of failing loudly — check the units and the fallback behaviour for unknown models.

categories.label: Host integrations
categories.why: Per-host surface (VS Code, CLI, Visual Studio, JetBrains, desktop). Confirm the change is mirrored where the hosts are expected to stay in sync, and that host-specific packaging still builds.

categories.label: Sharing server / stored data
categories.why: Server routes and the storage schema affect data already persisted for real users. Check for breaking schema changes and unvalidated request payloads.

categories.label: Dependencies
categories.why: New or bumped dependencies widen the supply-chain surface. Check that the manifest and the lockfile moved together and that no dependency was added without a reason in the PR body.

categories.label: Agent customizations
categories.why: Agents, skills, and instruction files steer every AI contributor on this repo. `.github/agents` ↔ `.claude/agents` and `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` ↔ `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` must change together (see AGENTS.md).

categories.label: Build tooling
categories.why: Build and lint configuration. Low blast radius on its own, but a broken build script blocks every other PR.

categories.label: Tests
categories.why: Test-only changes cannot break production behaviour, but deleted or weakened assertions can hide a regression — check that coverage went up, not down.

categories.label: Docs / assets
categories.why: Documentation, screenshots, and static assets. No runtime impact.
